newsitem.title: USA: BPA raises Thurs peak, firm power prices $1.50/MWh.
newsitem.headline: BPA raises Thurs peak, firm power prices $1.50/MWh.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) raised prices for firm power delivered during peak demand hours on Thursday by $1.50 per megawatt hour (MWh), the agency said Wednesday.
BPA still offered 300 megawatts of firm peak power, but raised prices to $15.50 per megawatt hour (MWh) for Northwest sales and $16.50 for California-Oregon border (COB) sales.
But prices for non-firm power during shoulder hours on Thursday (0600, 1100-1700 and 2100-2200 PST) were cut by $1.00 per MWh to $11.00 for Northwest and $12.00 for COB.
BPA continued to refrain from offering non-firm power during morning and evening peaks or any displacement power.
Prices for firm and non-firm power during off-peak hours on Thursday were unchanged at $9.00 per MWh for all deliveries.
